- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1-2 days) — cap forecast overshoot at +5–7% above immediate peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate rebound; add 1–2% upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag true trend by 1–3 days; if sentiment is bullish, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to 30d forecast.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often misses the turn — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% at the shift point.
- Avoid “flat” forecasts when sentiment is trending — even if price is stable, sentiment implies momentum; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias if sentiment > 0.5.
